newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil deputies begin voting on reform amendments.
newsitem.headline: Brazil deputies begin voting on reform amendments.

text.p: Brazil's Chamber of Deputies opened a session to vote on amendments to the government's civil service reform bill, an official said on Tuesday.

The first amendment to be considered is a proposal by an opposition party that would prevent state and municipal governments from setting pay and pension ceilings below a 10,800 real ($10,188) monthly cap, which the reform bill would establish.
Other amendments include a proposal by opposition parties that would entitle civil servants to maintain lifetime job guarantees, striking down one of the reform's main points.
Once voting on all amendments is completed, the reform bill may be put to a second and final vote on the floor of the lower house. If approved, the measure would advance to the Senate.
